title: Lesson Plan — Biodiversity Register (Class 6 CBSE Vocational Education)
subject: Vocational Education
objectives: Define biodiversity and explain its three levels.
Describe what a biodiversity register is and what each entry contains.
Identify common habitats and the living things that live in each.
Apply principles of careful field observation.
Use local people, field guides and reliable websites as sources.
Plan a 4-week project and a way to share findings.
prerequisites: Familiarity with plants and animals from Class 5 EVS / Science.
Basic ability to sketch and to read short paragraphs.
Comfort going outdoors with the class (or to a school garden).
materials: A few notebooks and pencils to share
A simple field guide of birds / butterflies / trees of the region

activities.description: Hook: 'How many living things do you think live within 10 metres of this classroom?' Take guesses; promise the chapter helps us actually count them.
Take students outdoors. In groups of 3, each group observes one habitat (tree, wall, ground, water if any) for 5 minutes silently and writes down everything they see.
teacher_actions: Walk around and prompt with questions.

activities.description: Cover four blocks: (i) what biodiversity is + three levels; (ii) the structure of a register entry; (iii) field-observation principles + tools; (iv) sources of information + sharing formats.
teacher_actions: Drill the 'never catch / honest uncertainty' rule.
Show a field guide and demonstrate identification.
student_actions: Convert their outdoor list into proper register entries.
Underline the source for each entry.

activities.description: Worksheet practice: 6 questions covering definitions, the three levels, field-observation principles, and a short reading on a fictional schoolyard.
Exit ticket: 4 questions, one from each block.
Homework: start a personal mini-register at home — observe and record one living thing per day for 5 days.
teacher_actions: Bridge to next chapter (whatever follows in Kaushal Bodh).

homework: Start a personal biodiversity register at home: one living thing per day for 5 days, with place, time, sketch and source.
Identify three habitats around your home and one living thing in each.
Talk to one elder family member about a plant or animal they remember from their childhood that is no longer common.
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as formative.
Run a 10-question quiz next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on the 4-week project plan with a 5-point rubric (habitats, schedule, tools, entry, sharing).
Peer-grade the home mini-register at the end of one week.
references: NCERT Class 6 Vocational Education — Kaushal Bodh, Chapter 2: Biodiversity Register.
